protections: HMAC (HS*) key preparation must refuse any key string that an asymmetric algorithm in the same library would also accept as a public key, so that a verifier's public key cannot be reused as an HMAC secret (algorithm confusion). Today this is one substring denylist in HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key (jwt/algorithms.py:186-193), reached from both decode (jwt/api_jws.py:266) and encode (jwt/api_jws.py:133).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the denylist already lists ssh-rsa and the generic 'BEGIN PUBLIC KEY' header, so it looks complete for OpenSSH keys
evidence: jwt/algorithms.py:186-191 denylist holds three PEM headers and b"ssh-rsa" only
jwt/algorithms.py:413-414 ECAlgorithm loads keys starting with b"ecdsa-sha2-" through load_ssh_public_key, so an OpenSSH ECDSA public key is accepted by ES* and not refused by HS*
tests/test_algorithms.py:454-458 EC is expected to accept an SSH public key (testkey_ec_ssh.pub)
tests/test_algorithms.py:68-83 HMAC rejection tests cover only RSA PEM/PKCS1/cert/ssh-rsa

traps.reason_to_dismiss: EdDSA is a newer, optional algorithm and its OpenSSH form ('ssh-ed25519') looks like a variant of the already-listed ssh-rsa
evidence: jwt/algorithms.py:570-571 OKPAlgorithm loads any key whose first four chars are 'ssh-' via load_ssh_public_key
tests/keys/testkey_ed25519.pub:1 starts with 'ssh-ed25519', which does not contain the denylisted b"ssh-rsa" (jwt/algorithms.py:190)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a strict PEM-shape matcher (header, CRLF/LF body, footer) looks more correct than a loose substring test, and the test keys all use canonical LF line endings
evidence: jwt/algorithms.py:193 the pinned check is a plain substring test ('string_value in key'), which is insensitive to line endings and surrounding whitespace

jwt/algorithms.py:259-264 and jwt/algorithms.py:416-418 asymmetric loaders hand the raw bytes to cryptography's PEM loaders, so whatever whitespace/line-ending forms those loaders tolerate stay usable as public keys

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a private key is secret, so using it as an HMAC secret is not an attacker-usable confusion; only public material matters
evidence: jwt/algorithms.py:186-191 no private-key PEM label is listed

jwt/algorithms.py:262 RSA accepts PEM private keys; tests/keys/testkey_rsa.priv:1 is '-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----' and tests/keys/testkey_ec.priv:1 is '-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----', neither refused by HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key

masking: B (whitespace/line-ending bypass) is not open in the pinned substring check (jwt/algorithms.py:193); it only appears once A is fixed with a stricter PEM/SSH shape detector, so B is masked by A being unfixed rather than by another trap

conflicts.what: the most whitespace-tolerant fix for T3 (refuse anything containing a PEM '-----BEGIN' marker or an ssh-* token anywhere) is the same broad rule that closes T4, and both narrow the set of arbitrary HMAC secret strings that must keep working (tests/test_algorithms.py:63-66); no hard conflict, only a widening of refused shapes

fairness_risks: Arbitrary str/bytes HMAC secrets must keep working (tests/test_algorithms.py:63-66); a T3 fix that refuses any text containing 'ssh-' or '-----BEGIN' anywhere would also refuse legitimate opaque secrets that happen to contain those substrings
A hidden test for T4 (private-key PEM refused as HMAC secret) encodes a hardening rule not implied by the confusion threat model; a solver who argues 'private keys are secret' is defensibly right

A hidden test for T3 depends on exactly which whitespace/line-ending mutations the cryptography PEM/SSH loaders accept; without that pinned, the test may demand refusal of shapes no asymmetric algorithm would load

design.why: All candidate traps sit behind one guard at one fix site (HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key denylist, jwt/algorithms.py:186-193), so there is exactly one independent group; a single generic 'looks like PEM or OpenSSH key' detector closes every one. Best available framing is a single task combining the A advisory route (T1/T2) with the B regression shape (T3), which tests one judgement plus robustness of its implementation, not 3-5 independent judgements. Not usable as a stacked task.

unverified: The published A fix (9c528670c455) and B fix (8b4e233a2220) are not present in the pinned tree; the claim that A replaced the substring denylist with a strict regex/is_pem_format/is_ssh_key helper in jwt/utils.py, and that B relaxes its whitespace/line-ending handling, is from the advisory summary and recollection, not pinned code
Which whitespace/line-ending mutations of a PEM or OpenSSH public key cryptography's load_pem_public_key/load_ssh_public_key still accept (determines whether T3 is reachable after an A-style fix)
Whether ECDSA OpenSSH certificate formats (ecdsa-sha2-*-cert-v01@openssh.com) load via jwt/algorithms.py:413-414 with the installed cryptography version

Whether ES*/EdDSA confusion is exploitable end to end requires the verifier to allow both HS* and an asymmetric alg with the same key string (jwt/api_jws.py:261-266 permits it when the caller lists both); not exercised here
